subject: Re: Post-call recap - model fit, evals, and regression next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@omniretail.com>, Tom Nguyen <tnguyen@omniretail.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-08T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap - model fit, evals, and next steps

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks for the time earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Key ask: improve OmniRetail’s FAQ/slot-filling accuracy and reduce hallucinations on product description prompts.
- What we saw on the call: your in-prod model (Redwood-v1.3) appears to have higher throughput but a measurable drop in slot-filling exact-match (you reported ~85% vs historical ~92%).
- Immediate risks: customer-facing responses with occasional incorrect attribute values; this is higher priority for your search-assisted experiences.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share the canonical prompt set you used in prod (attach if possible) — I’ve attached an updated eval prompt set we ran internally (omniretail_eval_promptset_v2.jsonl).
2) Run a quick model-diff/eval job against v1.2 (last known-good) and v1.3 (current) — I created an eval run you can view here: https://redwood.app/evals/OMNI-2026-42/run/7845.
3) If diffs confirm regression, we can pin your endpoint to v1.2 and roll-forward once we have mitigations. Marcus (engineering) and Neha (ML) are on cc to help with diffing and rollback.

Attachments: omniretail_eval_promptset_v2.jsonl (prompt set we recommend running), sample results dashboard link above.

Could you attach the production logs and any recent config changes for last week’s deploy? That will help us triage kernel/quantization changes quickly.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@omniretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap - model fit, evals, and next steps

Thanks Marissa —

Appreciate the clear plan. I attached the production logs from Oct 6-8 (production_error_logs_20261008.zip). We did flip from Redwood-v1.2 -> v1.3 last Tuesday to get better p99 latency; we started seeing higher hallucination reports in the field on Wednesday.

Numbers from our side (quick): exact-match for slot-filling fell from ~92% -> ~85% (sampled weekly test harness). We can tolerate a short pin/rollback window if needed, but we need to understand impact to throughput. Can we do a canary to prove a fix before a full rollback?

Also, can you confirm how long it would take to pin the endpoint to v1.2 and what the expected downtime (if any) is?

—Alicia
Senior Product Manager | OmniRetail
Alicia.Torres@omniretail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@omniretail.com>, Tom Nguyen <tnguyen@omniretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap - model fit, evals, and next steps

Great — thanks for the logs, Alicia. Looping in Marcus and Neha to propose technical next steps.

High-level plan we recommend:
- T0 (now): run the eval job I linked against your attached prompt set and our omniretail_eval_promptset_v2. We should get preliminary diffs within an hour for a 5k prompt pass.
- T+1: If diffs show regression (>=5-7% exact-match drop confirmed), we recommend pinning the endpoint to Redwood-v1.2 for customer traffic and creating a canary with v1.3 for comparison. Pinning is typically a config flip on the endpoint; no infra downtime — estimate 10–20 minutes to complete and validate.
- T+2: Marcus / infra to run a model-diff to identify which compilation/kernel/quantization changes map to the regression. Neha to run a targeted eval focusing on prompt categories where you saw degradation.

Can you confirm: 1) whether you want us to pin to v1.2 immediately if the diff confirms regression, and 2) whether you have a preferred maintenance window (evening US) for the config change?

We’ll prepare a rollback runbook and a short customer-facing statement you can use for communications.

—Marissa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@omniretail.com>, Tom Nguyen <tnguyen@omniretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap - model fit, evals, and next steps

Thanks — quick technical notes from infra/runtime: 

- Pin vs rollback: pinning the endpoint config to v1.2 (the last-good model) is a control-plane change. We can do that with zero infra downtime; clients will see the version flip at the next model fetch. Estimate 10–20m to deploy the config change and ~15–30m for warm-up depending on KV cache hit rate.
- Probable causes to look at: kernel selection and quantization profile changes between v1.2 -> v1.3 (we changed the fused-attention kernel in v1.3 on A100 pools). If that aligns with your timestamps, it’s a top suspect.
- I’ll run a model-diff (attached: model_diff_report.pdf) comparing activation stats, top-k token distributions, and per-prompt token probabilities.

If you want, we can initiate a pin immediately once Marissa/Alicia give the go-ahead; we’ll leave a canary in place for v1.3 for a graceful roll-forward once fixes land.

—Marcus
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@omniretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap - model fit, evals, and next steps

Attaching the eval artifacts and a preliminary diff summary (see model_diff_report.pdf) — attaching the prompt set we used (omniretail_eval_promptset_v2.jsonl). Quick notes: 

- Metric delta: slot-filling exact-match drop ~92% -> ~84.5% in our 5k sample for v1.3 vs v1.2. Highest impact on product attribute extraction and multi-slot dialogs.
- Observed model behavior: higher token perplexity spikes at attribute boundaries and an increase in low-confidence open-vocab fills (likely tied to quantize-induced probability smoothing).
- Recommended mitigations: revert/pin to v1.2 for production traffic, run targeted re-quantization with fallback to v1.2 quant profile, and add a lightweight heuristic post-filter for critical attributes for the short-term.

I’ve included sample per-prompt diffs in model_diff_report.pdf and uploaded the full artifacts to the drive link Marissa shared. I can run a fast 5k -> 50k batch overnight if you want broader coverage.

—Neha
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@omniretail.com>, Tom Nguyen <tnguyen@omniretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-09T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap - model fit, evals, and regression next steps

Thanks everyone — plan below and asks for Alicia: 

Plan
- We will pin your production endpoint to Redwood-v1.2 now that diffs confirm regression (Neha + Marcus to execute). Expect ~10–20m control-plane flip + 15–30m warm-up; no infra downtime.
- Keep a v1.3 canary running against a subset of traffic for monitoring and regression debugging.
- Neha to run extended 50k eval overnight and share per-category breakdown by tomorrow EOD.

Alicia — can you confirm you’re OK with the pin now? Also confirm whether you want us to perform the change during this afternoon window (US business hours) or in your preferred evening maintenance window. Once you confirm we’ll schedule the config flip and share the rollback runbook and customer statement.

If you’d like a 30-minute sync to walk through the diff report and the proposed post-filter approach, we can do 4pm PT today.

—Marissa
